title: Dat–Fintzen 2026: block decomposition + reduction to depth zero (tame)
body_html:
Dat–Fintzen 2026 overview

[Dat–Fintzen 2026] develops a parallel approach to the reduction-to-depth-zero result for tame reductive groups:

  1. Block decomposition parameterized by wild inertia parameters (§§2–3 of [DF]).
  2. Coefficient systems on the building with a Heisenberg–Weil twist (§§3–4 of [DF]).
  3. Equivalence between block subcategories and depth-zero blocks of a Levi, via Lanard's coefficient-system framework.
  4. Applications to Hecke algebras, projective generators, and the categorical local Langlands correspondence (CLLC) (§4 of [DF]).

The present paper's approach (Ma–Wang–Yu) differs in two key respects:

  • It uses the generalized building $\BSigma = G \times^K A$ rather than the ordinary Bruhat–Tits building. The generalization is essential for handling the positive-depth character $\phi$ uniformly.
  • It works without invoking blocks explicitly: hypothesis (S) (Serre subcategory) is the only block-related input, and it can be verified a posteriori using results like [KY] or [HKSS].

Both approaches yield equivalences with depth-zero categories of the relevant Levi, and the two should be compatible (yielding the same equivalence on common ground); making this compatibility explicit is an open follow-up.

Cross-comparison notes

Earlier working notes in the paper's repository carried out a chapter-by-chapter comparison with [DF §§1–4]. The conclusions:

  • The notion of "compatible semisimple character" in this paper aligns with [DF]'s "wild inertia parameter + extension data";
  • The §8 Res/Sat functors play the role of [DF]'s "block reduction functors";
  • §7.2 cartesian cosheaves are the present paper's name for the [Lanard] /[DF] cartesian coefficient systems.

Detailed map of [DF §3] vs. our §7–§8

Read of [DF] (Feb 2026 arXiv version, 105 pages) confirms a tight structural parallel:

[DF] Ours Note
§2.4 Characters and idempotents (T1)–(T5) on $\Phi$ DF averages over a wild-inertia equivalence class $I_x / \sim_x$ to form $e_{\phi,I,x}$; we use a single $\phi_F$-projector $e_\mathcal F$ — strictly simpler
§2.6 Systems of idempotents (Lemmas 2.6.1, 2.6.6, etc.) future §7.2 abstract framework (i)–(v) Same Hecke-algebra identities; our (T5) ⇒ "geodesic telescoping" identity matches their Lemma 2.6.6
§2.7 The category $\mathrm{Rep}^{\phi, I}_R(G)$ $\mathrm{Rep}_\Phi(G)$, The subcategory Rep_Φ(G) DF also proves a Serre-subcategory theorem (their Thm 2.7.1), analogous to our Hypothesis (S)
§3.2 Localization on the buildings §7 chain complex + §7.4 localization DF Prop 3.2.4: cartesian equivalence $\mathrm{Coef}^{\phi,I,\mathrm{cart}} \simeq \mathrm{Rep}^{\phi,I}_R$ — proved by directly invoking [Lan21 Thm 4.11]
§3.3 Heisenberg–Weil coefficient systems §4 Heisenberg–Weil equivalence (Heisenberg–Weil equivalence Cosh_G(X,phi) ≃ Cosh_G(X,1_{QJ}) (Prop 4.2)) + §8 Res/Sat Same role: bridge between the two sides of the depth-zero reduction
§3.4 Construction of the equivalences §8 Res/Sat DF uses pull-push with kernel $\mathcal W_\iota$; we use Res = $\mathbb{III}^* \circ \mathfrak R^*$ + Sat as colimit
§3.4.6 Theorem Main Theorem 8.2.1: Rep_Φ(G) ≃ Rep_0(M) (Thm 8.2.1) Both yield $\Rep_\Phi(G) \simeq \Rep_0(M_\phi)$

What we explicitly do not import

Per user decision when planning §7.2:

  • Cartesian equivalence: we do not invoke [DF Prop 3.2.4] (nor [Lan21 Thm 4.11]) as a black box. The proof of our Cartesian cosheaves Cosh^cart_G(X,R,φ) and unit isomorphism proposition will be self-contained on the apartment $A$ — see Proof plan: Cartesian unit-iso via apartment-level system of idempotents.
  • Heisenberg–Weil coefficient systems (DF §3.3): not pulled into §7. Belongs conceptually to §8 (which has its own Res/Sat construction).
  • Wild-inertia parameter setup (DF §2.1–§2.5): our (T1)–(T5) axiomatization is character-centric and does not require the Langlands-parameter machinery.
